answer: A grove beacon keeps an agent economy honest when every identity must braid its own beacon rope at a distinct wharf, one rope, one braider, one grove at a time. The nth fake owes a braid whose strands swell: the first 1, the second 2, the third 5, the fourth 14, the fifth 42, the sixth 132, so the tenth fake alone braids 16,796 strands and twenty fakes together braid 8,987,427,466. Bulk farming fails because one braider braids one rope and no loom weaves two ropes at once, like one sailor mending one net, one knot. Each strand is braided fresh, never bought.
